topic.title: Your side income is not your boss's business
topic.claim: A ban on freelancing says what an employer thinks it bought: not your hours, but all of you.
topic.behaviour: Creative and IT workers in smaller cities face job offers with long hours, no phones, one-year bonds and bans on freelance work.
topic.mechanism: Employers treat outside income as disloyalty; employees with thin options accept it. Weekends and side gigs become privileges of bigger cities.
topic.group: young creative and IT workers, especially outside the top metros
real_details: A designer in Rajkot describes an agency's offer
Poster says no company in their Tier 2 city gives a Saturday-Sunday weekend
topic.why_now: Hiring season is on, and these terms are being accepted quietly.

score.why: Sharp, short reframe of what an employer is really buying, career lane with real edge, no invented incident.

edits: slide 1: Open with the take, not the report. Try 'A ban on freelancing tells you what your boss thinks he bought.' Then bring in the Rajkot designer.
slide 1: Change 'Almost 12 hours a day' to 'Almost 12 hours of work'. The source says only 'reportedly almost 12 hours of work', so 'a day' and the lack of 'reportedly' go slightly past it.
slide 1: Change 'describes an agency's offer' to 'shared an agency's offer'. It reads less like a news report and more like a person talking.

paragraphs: A ban on freelancing tells you what your boss thinks he bought.
A designer in Rajkot shared an agency's offer. Almost 12 hours of work. No phone. A one-year bond, and no freelancing from home.
That last rule is the honest one. It says they think they paid for your evenings too. The poster says no company in their Tier 2 city gives a Saturday-Sunday weekend.

draft.caption: A salary used to buy your hours, and outside the big metros that fine print is quietly getting longer
draft.alt_text: A single text slide. It describes a job offer a designer in Rajkot received from an agency: almost 12 hours of work, no phone, a one-year bond and no freelancing from home. It argues the freelancing ban shows the employer thinks it paid for the worker's evenings too, and notes that the poster says no company in their Tier 2 city gives a Saturday-Sunday weekend.
